title: Sampling Distributions
text:
Set a sample size, then draw sample after sample from the same population. Each sample gives you one mean, one SS, one variance, one SD — and those values pile up into a distribution of their own. That pile is the sampling distribution.

#| '!! shinylive warning !!': |
#|   shinylive does not work in self-contained HTML documents.
#|   Please set `embed-resources: false` in your metadata.
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 1050

from shiny import App, render, ui, reactive
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

C_BAR = "darkorange"    # every histogram on this page
C_OBS = "purple"        # the observed average of whatever the panel shows
C_DATA = "dodgerblue"
C_TRUE = "black"

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.layout_sidebar(
        ui.sidebar(
            ui.input_select(
                "dist", "Population shape",
                {"norm": "Normal (symmetric, bell)",
                 "unif": "Uniform (flat)",
                 "exp": "Exponential (right-skewed)",
                 "bimodal": "Bimodal (two peaks)",
                 "beta": "Beta (left-skewed)"}
            ),
            ui.input_numeric("pop_mu", "Population mean (μ):", value=100.0, step=1.0),
            ui.input_numeric("pop_var", "Population variance (σ²):", value=225.0,
                             min=0.1, step=5.0),
            ui.input_numeric("n", "Sample size (n):", value=10, min=2, step=1),
            ui.hr(),
            ui.input_action_button("draw_1", "Draw 1 sample", class_="btn-primary"),
            ui.input_action_button("draw_10", "Draw 10", class_="btn-success"),
            ui.input_action_button("draw_100", "Draw 100", class_="btn-warning"),
            ui.input_action_button("reset", "Clear", class_="btn-danger"),
            ui.hr(),
            ui.output_ui("readout"),
            width=300
        ),
        ui.output_plot("main_plot", height="1000px")
    )
)


def server(input, output, session):
    hist = reactive.Value({"means": [], "ss": [], "var": [], "sd": []})

    def base_params(d):
        return {"norm": (0.0, 1.0),
                "unif": (0.5, np.sqrt(1 / 12)),
                "exp": (1.0, 1.0),
                "bimodal": (0.0, np.sqrt(4.25)),
                "beta": (0.8, np.sqrt(16 / 1100))}[d]

    def draw_samples(k):
        d = input.dist()
        mu, sigma = float(input.pop_mu()), np.sqrt(float(input.pop_var()))
        n = int(input.n())
        b_mu, b_sigma = base_params(d)
        size = (k, n)
        if d == "norm":
            raw = np.random.standard_normal(size)
        elif d == "unif":
            raw = np.random.uniform(size=size)
        elif d == "exp":
            raw = np.random.exponential(size=size)
        elif d == "bimodal":
            raw = np.random.normal(np.where(np.random.rand(k, n) < 0.5, -2, 2), 0.5)
        else:
            raw = np.random.beta(8, 2, size=size)
        x = (raw - b_mu) * (sigma / b_sigma) + mu

        means = x.mean(axis=1)
        ss = np.sum((x - means[:, None]) ** 2, axis=1)
        var = ss / (n - 1)
        sd = np.sqrt(var)

        cur = hist.get().copy()
        cur["means"] = cur["means"] + means.tolist()
        cur["ss"] = cur["ss"] + ss.tolist()
        cur["var"] = cur["var"] + var.tolist()
        cur["sd"] = cur["sd"] + sd.tolist()
        hist.set(cur)

    @reactive.Effect
    @reactive.event(input.draw_1)
    def _d1():
        draw_samples(1)

    @reactive.Effect
    @reactive.event(input.draw_10)
    def _d10():
        draw_samples(10)

    @reactive.Effect
    @reactive.event(input.draw_100)
    def _d100():
        draw_samples(100)

    @reactive.Effect
    @reactive.event(input.reset, input.dist, input.pop_mu, input.pop_var, input.n)
    def _clear():
        hist.set({"means": [], "ss": [], "var": [], "sd": []})

    def pop_curve(d, mu, sigma):
        x = np.linspace(mu - 4 * sigma, mu + 4 * sigma, 800)
        b_mu, b_sigma = base_params(d)
        scale = sigma / b_sigma
        xb = (x - mu) / scale + b_mu
        if d == "norm":
            yb = np.exp(-0.5 * xb ** 2) / np.sqrt(2 * np.pi)
        elif d == "unif":
            yb = np.where((xb >= 0) & (xb <= 1), 1.0, 0.0)
        elif d == "exp":
            yb = np.where(xb >= 0, np.exp(-xb), 0.0)
        elif d == "bimodal":
            yb = (np.exp(-2 * (xb + 2) ** 2) + np.exp(-2 * (xb - 2) ** 2)) / np.sqrt(2 * np.pi)
        else:
            yb = np.where((xb >= 0) & (xb <= 1), 72 * xb ** 7 * (1 - xb), 0.0)
        return x, yb / scale

    @output
    @render.ui
    def readout():
        h = hist.get()
        k = len(h["means"])
        if k == 0:
            return ui.markdown("*No samples yet.*")
        n = int(input.n())
        sigma = np.sqrt(float(input.pop_var()))
        return ui.markdown(
            f"**{k} samples of n = {n}**  \n"
            f"mean of M = {np.mean(h['means']):.2f}  \n"
            f"mean of SS = {np.mean(h['ss']):.1f}  \n"
            f"mean of s² = {np.mean(h['var']):.2f}  \n"
            f"mean of s = {np.mean(h['sd']):.2f}  (σ = {sigma:.2f})")

    @output
    @render.plot
    def main_plot():
        h = hist.get()
        k = len(h["means"])
        d = input.dist()
        mu = float(input.pop_mu())
        true_var = float(input.pop_var())
        sigma = np.sqrt(true_var)
        n = int(input.n())

        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12, 11))
        gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 2, height_ratios=[0.9, 1, 1], hspace=0.42, wspace=0.26)
        ax_pop = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :])
        ax_mean = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
        ax_ss = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
        ax_var = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
        ax_sd = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])

        x, y = pop_curve(d, mu, sigma)
        ax_pop.plot(x, y, color="gray", lw=2)
        ax_pop.fill_between(x, y, alpha=0.2, color="gray")
        ax_pop.axvline(mu, color=C_TRUE, ls="--", lw=2, label=f"μ = {mu:g}")
        ax_pop.set_xlim(mu - 4 * sigma, mu + 4 * sigma)
        ax_pop.set_title(f"Population — every sample of n = {n} comes from here")
        ax_pop.legend(loc="upper right")

        panels = [(ax_mean, "Sampling distribution of M"),
                  (ax_ss, "Sampling distribution of SS"),
                  (ax_var, "Sampling distribution of s²"),
                  (ax_sd, "Sampling distribution of s")]
        if k == 0:
            for ax, title in panels:
                ax.set_title(title)
                ax.text(0.5, 0.5, "Draw some samples", ha="center", va="center",
                        transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=12, color="gray")
                ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
            return fig

        bins = min(30, max(8, int(np.sqrt(k))))

        # mean: centres on mu, spread is the standard error
        ax_mean.hist(h["means"], bins=bins, density=True, color=C_BAR,
                     edgecolor="white", alpha=0.75)
        se = sigma / np.sqrt(n)
        xm = np.linspace(mu - 4 * se, mu + 4 * se, 300)
        ax_mean.plot(xm, np.exp(-0.5 * ((xm - mu) / se) ** 2) / (se * np.sqrt(2 * np.pi)),
                     color="seagreen", lw=2, label=r"$N(\mu,\ \sigma^2/n)$")
        ax_mean.axvline(mu, color=C_TRUE, ls="--", lw=2, label=f"μ = {mu:g}")
        ax_mean.axvline(np.mean(h["means"]), color=C_OBS, lw=2,
                        label=f"mean of M = {np.mean(h['means']):.2f}")
        ax_mean.set_title(f"M over {k} samples — centres on μ, SE = {se:.2f}")
        ax_mean.set_xlabel("sample mean M")
        ax_mean.legend(loc="upper right")

        # SS: expectation is (n-1) sigma^2
        ax_ss.hist(h["ss"], bins=bins, color=C_BAR, edgecolor="white", alpha=0.75)
        exp_ss = (n - 1) * true_var
        ax_ss.axvline(exp_ss, color=C_TRUE, ls="--", lw=2,
                      label=f"$(n-1)\\sigma^2$ = {exp_ss:.0f}")
        ax_ss.axvline(np.mean(h["ss"]), color=C_OBS, lw=2,
                      label=f"mean of SS = {np.mean(h['ss']):.0f}")
        ax_ss.set_title("SS — depends on n, so it has no fixed target")
        ax_ss.set_xlabel(r"$\sum (X-M)^2$")
        ax_ss.legend(loc="upper right")

        # variance: unbiased, averages to sigma^2
        ax_var.hist(h["var"], bins=bins, color=C_BAR, edgecolor="white", alpha=0.75)
        ax_var.axvline(true_var, color=C_TRUE, ls="--", lw=2, label=f"σ² = {true_var:g}")
        ax_var.axvline(np.mean(h["var"]), color=C_OBS, lw=2,
                       label=f"mean of s² = {np.mean(h['var']):.1f}")
        ax_var.set_title("s² is unbiased — its average lands on σ²")
        ax_var.set_xlabel(r"$s^2$")
        ax_var.legend(loc="upper right")

        # sd: NOT unbiased, averages a little below sigma
        ax_sd.hist(h["sd"], bins=bins, color=C_BAR, edgecolor="white", alpha=0.75)
        ax_sd.axvline(sigma, color=C_TRUE, ls="--", lw=2, label=f"σ = {sigma:.2f}")
        ax_sd.axvline(np.mean(h["sd"]), color=C_OBS, lw=2,
                      label=f"mean of s = {np.mean(h['sd']):.2f}")
        ax_sd.set_title("s sits slightly below σ on average")
        ax_sd.set_xlabel(r"$s$")
        ax_sd.legend(loc="upper right")

        return fig


app = App(app_ui, server)


What to look for

M piles up into a bell curve centred on \(\mu\), whatever shape the population has — that is the Central Limit Theorem. Its spread is the standard error, \(\sigma/\sqrt{n}\), so raise \(n\) and the pile narrows.
SS has no fixed target. Change \(n\) and the whole distribution slides, because SS is a total. Its average sits at \((n-1)\sigma^2\).
s² is unbiased: draw enough samples and the average of all your \(s^2\) values lands on \(\sigma^2\). This is what dividing by \(n-1\) buys you.
s is the interesting one. Even though \(s^2\) averages to \(\sigma^2\), the average of \(s\) lands slightly below \(\sigma\) — taking a square root does not preserve the unbiasedness. Try a small \(n\), like 2 or 3, and the gap is easy to see.

title: PSYC 220 — Interactive Demos
text:
Two demos, both about the same four numbers: the mean (M), the sum of squares (SS), the variance (s²), and the standard deviation (s).
Everything runs in your browser — nothing to install, and nothing you do here is recorded.

1. Growing a Sample
Add scores to a sample one at a time and watch all four statistics update.
The thing to notice is that they do not behave the same way. The mean settles on \(\mu\). The variance and SD settle too. But SS just keeps climbing, because it is a total rather than an average — which is exactly why SS on its own cannot tell you whether one group is more spread out than another.


2. Sampling Distributions
Fix a sample size, then draw sample after sample. Each one hands you a mean, an SS, a variance and an SD, and those values stack up into distributions of their own.
Three things fall out of it: sample means form a bell curve centred on \(\mu\) whatever the population looks like (the Central Limit Theorem); the spread of that curve is the standard error, \(\sigma/\sqrt{n}\); and \(s^2\) averages out to exactly \(\sigma^2\), which is what dividing by \(n-1\) is for.






TipTry to break them



Pick the exponential or bimodal population and set \(n = 2\). The population is nothing like a bell curve, but keep drawing and watch what the distribution of sample means does anyway. Then raise \(n\) and watch it tighten.

title: Growing a Sample
text:
Draw scores one at a time from a population you choose, and watch four statistics update as the sample grows. The population values you set are the truth; the sample statistics are estimates of them, and the point of the demo is to see how each one behaves as \(n\) increases.

#| '!! shinylive warning !!': |
#|   shinylive does not work in self-contained HTML documents.
#|   Please set `embed-resources: false` in your metadata.
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 1050

from shiny import App, render, ui, reactive
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

C_MU = "purple"        # anything computed about the population mean, mu
C_M = "darkorange"     # anything computed about the sample mean, M
C_DATA = "dodgerblue"
C_TRUE = "black"

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.layout_sidebar(
        ui.sidebar(
            ui.input_select(
                "dist", "Population shape",
                {"norm": "Normal (symmetric, bell)",
                 "unif": "Uniform (flat)",
                 "exp": "Exponential (right-skewed)",
                 "bimodal": "Bimodal (two peaks)",
                 "beta": "Beta (left-skewed)"}
            ),
            ui.input_numeric("pop_mu", "Population mean (μ):", value=100.0, step=1.0),
            ui.input_numeric("pop_var", "Population variance (σ²):", value=225.0,
                             min=0.1, step=5.0),
            ui.hr(),
            ui.input_action_button("draw_1", "Add 1 score", class_="btn-primary"),
            ui.input_action_button("draw_10", "Add 10 scores", class_="btn-success"),
            ui.input_action_button("reset", "Start over", class_="btn-danger"),
            ui.hr(),
            ui.input_checkbox("show_m", "Deviations about M (sample mean)", value=True),
            ui.input_checkbox("show_mu", "Deviations about μ (population mean)", value=False),
            ui.hr(),
            ui.output_ui("readout"),
            width=300
        ),
        ui.output_plot("main_plot", height="1000px")
    )
)


def server(input, output, session):
    sample_data = reactive.Value([])

    # mean and sd of each raw distribution, before it is shifted and scaled
    def base_params(d):
        return {"norm": (0.0, 1.0),
                "unif": (0.5, np.sqrt(1 / 12)),
                "exp": (1.0, 1.0),
                "bimodal": (0.0, np.sqrt(4.25)),
                "beta": (0.8, np.sqrt(16 / 1100))}[d]

    def draw(k):
        d = input.dist()
        mu, sigma = float(input.pop_mu()), np.sqrt(float(input.pop_var()))
        b_mu, b_sigma = base_params(d)
        if d == "norm":
            raw = np.random.standard_normal(k)
        elif d == "unif":
            raw = np.random.uniform(size=k)
        elif d == "exp":
            raw = np.random.exponential(size=k)
        elif d == "bimodal":
            raw = np.random.normal(np.where(np.random.rand(k) < 0.5, -2, 2), 0.5)
        else:
            raw = np.random.beta(8, 2, size=k)
        return ((raw - b_mu) * (sigma / b_sigma) + mu).tolist()

    @reactive.Effect
    @reactive.event(input.draw_1)
    def _add1():
        sample_data.set(sample_data() + draw(1))

    @reactive.Effect
    @reactive.event(input.draw_10)
    def _add10():
        sample_data.set(sample_data() + draw(10))

    @reactive.Effect
    @reactive.event(input.reset, input.dist, input.pop_mu, input.pop_var)
    def _clear():
        sample_data.set([])

    def pop_curve(d, mu, sigma):
        x = np.linspace(mu - 4 * sigma, mu + 4 * sigma, 800)
        b_mu, b_sigma = base_params(d)
        scale = sigma / b_sigma
        xb = (x - mu) / scale + b_mu
        if d == "norm":
            yb = np.exp(-0.5 * xb ** 2) / np.sqrt(2 * np.pi)
        elif d == "unif":
            yb = np.where((xb >= 0) & (xb <= 1), 1.0, 0.0)
        elif d == "exp":
            yb = np.where(xb >= 0, np.exp(-xb), 0.0)
        elif d == "bimodal":
            yb = (np.exp(-2 * (xb + 2) ** 2) + np.exp(-2 * (xb - 2) ** 2)) / np.sqrt(2 * np.pi)
        else:
            yb = np.where((xb >= 0) & (xb <= 1), 72 * xb ** 7 * (1 - xb), 0.0)
        return x, yb / scale

    @output
    @render.ui
    def readout():
        data = np.array(sample_data())
        n = len(data)
        if n == 0:
            return ui.markdown("*No scores yet.*")
        m = data.mean()
        ss = float(np.sum((data - m) ** 2))
        if n > 1:
            var = ss / (n - 1)
            return ui.markdown(
                f"**n = {n}**  \nM = {m:.2f}  \nSS = {ss:.1f}  \n"
                f"s² = {var:.2f}  \ns = {np.sqrt(var):.2f}")
        ss_mu = float((data[0] - float(input.pop_mu())) ** 2)
        return ui.markdown(
            f"**n = 1**  \nM = {m:.2f}  \n"
            f"SS about M = 0  \nSS about μ = {ss_mu:.1f}  \n"
            f"*s² and s need n ≥ 2*")

    @output
    @render.plot
    def main_plot():
        data = np.array(sample_data())
        n = len(data)
        d = input.dist()
        mu = float(input.pop_mu())
        true_var = float(input.pop_var())
        sigma = np.sqrt(true_var)
        show_mu = bool(input.show_mu())
        show_m = bool(input.show_m())

        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12, 11))
        gs = fig.add_gridspec(3, 2, height_ratios=[0.9, 1, 1], hspace=0.42, wspace=0.26)
        ax_pop = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, :])
        ax_mean = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0])
        ax_ss = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])
        ax_var = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 0])
        ax_sd = fig.add_subplot(gs[2, 1])

        x, y = pop_curve(d, mu, sigma)
        ax_pop.plot(x, y, color="gray", lw=2)
        ax_pop.fill_between(x, y, alpha=0.2, color="gray")
        ax_pop.axvline(mu, color=C_TRUE, ls="--", lw=2, label=f"μ = {mu:g}")
        ax_pop.set_xlim(mu - 4 * sigma, mu + 4 * sigma)
        ax_pop.set_title("Population, and the scores drawn so far")
        if n:
            ax_pop.scatter(data, np.zeros(n), color=C_DATA, zorder=5, alpha=0.6, label="scores")
            ax_pop.axvline(data.mean(), color=C_M, lw=2, label=f"M = {data.mean():.2f}")
        ax_pop.legend(loc="upper right")

        panels = [(ax_mean, "Sample mean M"), (ax_ss, "Sum of squares SS"),
                  (ax_var, "Variance"), (ax_sd, "Standard deviation")]
        if n == 0:
            for ax, title in panels:
                ax.set_title(title)
                ax.text(0.5, 0.5, "Add a score to begin", ha="center", va="center",
                        transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=12, color="gray")
                ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([])
            return fig

        ns = np.arange(1, n + 1)
        means, ss_mu, ss_m, var_n1, var_n, sd_n1, sd_n = [], [], [], [], [], [], []
        for i in ns:
            sub = data[:i]
            m = sub.mean()
            means.append(m)
            ss_mu.append(np.sum((sub - mu) ** 2))
            s_m = np.sum((sub - m) ** 2)
            ss_m.append(s_m)
            var_n.append(np.sum((sub - mu) ** 2) / i)
            var_n1.append(s_m / (i - 1) if i > 1 else np.nan)
            sd_n.append(np.sqrt(var_n[-1]))
            sd_n1.append(np.sqrt(var_n1[-1]) if i > 1 else np.nan)

        # mean
        ax_mean.axhline(mu, color=C_TRUE, ls="--", lw=2, label=f"μ = {mu:g}")
        ax_mean.plot(ns, means, color=C_M, marker="o", ms=3, label="M")
        ax_mean.set_title("Sample mean settles on μ")
        ax_mean.set_xlabel("n"); ax_mean.set_ylabel("M")
        ax_mean.legend(loc="upper right")

        # SS -- the one that grows without bound
        if show_mu:
            ax_ss.plot(ns, ss_mu, color=C_MU, marker="o", ms=3, label=r"$\sum (X-\mu)^2$")
        if show_m:
            ax_ss.plot(ns, ss_m, color=C_M, marker="s", ms=3, label=r"$\sum (X-M)^2$")
        ax_ss.set_title("SS keeps growing — it is a total")
        ax_ss.set_xlabel("n"); ax_ss.set_ylabel("SS")
        if show_mu or show_m:
            ax_ss.legend(loc="upper left")

        # variance
        ax_var.axhline(true_var, color=C_TRUE, ls="--", lw=2, label=f"σ² = {true_var:g}")
        shown = []
        if show_mu:
            ax_var.plot(ns, var_n, color=C_MU, marker="o", ms=3, alpha=0.8,
                        label=r"$\sum (X-\mu)^2 / n$")
            shown += list(var_n)
        if show_m and n > 1:
            ax_var.plot(ns, var_n1, color=C_M, marker="s", ms=3, alpha=0.8,
                        label=r"$\sum (X-M)^2 / (n-1)$")
            shown += list(var_n1)
        elif show_m:
            ax_var.text(0.5, 0.08, "needs n ≥ 2", ha="center", color="gray",
                        transform=ax_var.transAxes, fontsize=10)
        ax_var.set_title("Variance is an average — it settles")
        ax_var.set_xlabel("n"); ax_var.set_ylabel("variance")
        vals = [v for v in shown if np.isfinite(v)] + [true_var]
        ax_var.set_ylim(0, max(vals) * 1.35)
        ax_var.legend(loc="upper right")

        # sd
        ax_sd.axhline(sigma, color=C_TRUE, ls="--", lw=2, label=f"σ = {sigma:.2f}")
        shown = []
        if show_mu:
            ax_sd.plot(ns, sd_n, color=C_MU, marker="o", ms=3, alpha=0.8,
                       label=r"$\sqrt{\sum (X-\mu)^2 / n}$")
            shown += list(sd_n)
        if show_m and n > 1:
            ax_sd.plot(ns, sd_n1, color=C_M, marker="s", ms=3, alpha=0.8,
                       label=r"$\sqrt{\sum (X-M)^2 / (n-1)}$")
            shown += list(sd_n1)
        elif show_m:
            ax_sd.text(0.5, 0.08, "needs n ≥ 2", ha="center", color="gray",
                       transform=ax_sd.transAxes, fontsize=10)
        ax_sd.set_title("SD is the variance back in the original units")
        ax_sd.set_xlabel("n"); ax_sd.set_ylabel("SD")
        vals = [v for v in shown if np.isfinite(v)] + [sigma]
        ax_sd.set_ylim(0, max(vals) * 1.35)
        ax_sd.legend(loc="upper right")

        return fig


app = App(app_ui, server)


What to look for

M wanders at first and then settles on \(\mu\). With a handful of scores it can be well off.
SS never settles — it climbs with every score you add, because it is a total, not an average. That is why SS on its own cannot tell you whether one group is more spread out than another.
Variance does settle, because dividing by \(n\) (or \(n-1\)) turns the total into an average.
SD settles too, and in the same units as the original scores — which is why it is the one you report.

The purple and orange curves differ only in which mean the deviations are taken from. The orange one is always the smaller of the two, because \(M\) is the value that makes \(\sum (X-c)^2\) as small as it can be.
